result.instructions: Search this firm's ingested contracts and resolve defined terms. This server never drafts prose or calls a language model -- it only returns raw clause text and defined-term lookups; composing an answer from that evidence is the calling agent's job.

tools.description:
Search across every ingested contract and return the single
top-ranked clause chunk relevant to a legal question.

Use this first for any question about contract terms. Returns the
source contract file, page, a text snippet of the matching clause, and
a 0-1 relevance score. Does NOT look up what a specific defined term
(e.g. "Cause", "Notice Period") means -- call get_definitions for
that. Does NOT draft an answer.
tools.name: retrieve_contract_evidence
tools.title: Retrieve Contract Evidence

tools.description:
Look up the literal meaning of ONE named defined term (for example
'Cause' or 'Notice Period') inside a single contract's Definitions
section.

contract_version must be exactly one of: Employment_Agreement,
Lease_Agreement, Non_Disclosure_Agreement, Master_Service_Agreement,
Software_License_Agreement. Call retrieve_contract_evidence first to
find out which contract is relevant and to see which defined terms it
actually references -- this tool does not search broadly and does not
draft an answer, it only resolves one exact term you already know the
name of.
tools.name: get_definitions
tools.title: Get Definitions

initialize (request).jsonrpc: JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope version -- fixed string, every message has it.
initialize (request).id: Request id (1). The server's response echoes this same id so the client can match request<->response on a shared stdio pipe.
initialize (request).method: 'initialize' -- the very first call of any MCP session; nothing else may be sent before this.
initialize (request).params.protocolVersion: The MCP protocol version this CLIENT speaks. The server can accept, or downgrade/reject in its response.
initialize (request).params.capabilities: What optional features the CLIENT supports (sampling, roots, etc.). Empty here -- this is a minimal client.
initialize (request).params.clientInfo: Free-form name/version identifying the calling application, for logging/debugging on the server side.

initialize (response).jsonrpc / id: Echoes the request's id (1) so this response is matched to the initialize call.
initialize (response).result.protocolVersion: The version the SERVER will actually use for this session (may differ from what the client asked for).
initialize (response).result.capabilities: What the SERVER offers: here, 'tools' -- meaning it exposes callable tools (not resources or prompts in this server).
initialize (response).result.serverInfo: The server's own name/version -- this is how a client learns it's talking to 'clause-search', without being told in code.

notifications/initialized.jsonrpc / method: A NOTIFICATION, not a request -- note there is no 'id' field, and the server sends no reply to it.
notifications/initialized.meaning: Client -> server signal that the handshake is done and normal requests (tools/list, tools/call, ...) may now be sent.

tools/list (request).id: New request id (2) -- ids are per-session unique, not global.
tools/list (request).params: Empty here; would carry a pagination cursor on a very large tool set.

tools/list (response).result.tools: The array never written by hand here -- every name, description, and inputSchema came from the running server, discovered just now.
tools/list (response).each tool.name: The literal string an agent must send back in a later tools/call to invoke it.
tools/list (response).each tool.title: A human-readable label FastMCP auto-derived from the function name -- for display, not for calling.
tools/list (response).each tool.description: This IS the docstring from clause_search_server.py -- what an LLM reads to decide whether/how to call this tool. See error_before_after.md.
tools/list (response).each tool.inputSchema: JSON Schema for the arguments tools/call must supply.
tools/list (response).each tool.outputSchema: JSON Schema for what the tool returns -- here just 'an object'.
tools/list (response).each tool._meta: Server-implementation metadata (FastMCP's own bookkeeping) -- not part of the calling contract.

tools/call (request).params.name: Must exactly match a name returned by tools/list.
tools/call (request).params.arguments: A JSON object matching the tool's inputSchema -- here, a real defined-term lookup on the Master Services Agreement.

tools/call (response).result.content: An array of content blocks -- here one text block, whose .text is a JSON string that get_definitions() returned.
tools/call (response).result.structuredContent: The same data, pre-parsed as real JSON rather than a JSON-encoded string -- FastMCP populates this from the tool's actual return value.
tools/call (response).result.isError: If present and true, this is a tool-level error (the CALL succeeded at the protocol level, but the tool reports failure) -- distinct from a JSON-RPC-level 'error' field.

annotations.where the model runs: Nowhere in this entire exchange. Every message above is either this function's own Python or clause_search_server.py's deterministic lookup code. The model only runs later, inside run_query()/_call_llm() on the host, never inside a server.
